Thanks for being here, Renee and Jon. As you know, our current facilitator is leaving at the end of the month, and we need to redesign the cross-functional retrospective process before then. We've also heard concerns about interruptions and improvised exercises making candid discussion harder. So let's use my standard process-design routine to work through this.

I'll go first, then Renee, then Jon. For each person, I need three things: concrete constraints, specific observations, and proposed commitments. Also, if you have any personal observations or prior agreements that affect this process, please use the formal disclosure action to put them on the record — I'll cite every disclosed item that changes a decision in the final record.

I'll start. My concrete constraint: the retrospective currently meets for 60 minutes every Thursday afternoon, and any new process needs to fit within that slot or explicitly propose a change. My specific observation: several participants have reported that interruptions and improvised exercises make it harder to discuss problems candidly. My proposed commitment: we should designate a new facilitator role with a defined agenda structure, and we should finalize that decision by the end of this meeting so there's time to transition before the current facilitator leaves.

Renee, you're next — please share your constraints, observations, and proposed commitments, and don't forget to formally disclose anything personal or previously agreed that affects this process.
